ai.literal: Not being despised he who desires he who is called, of whatever measure even one thing, not stealing let him guard his mind.
ai.translation: He who wishes to live without being despised must guard his mind against even the slightest thought of stealing.
ai.modern: பிறரால் இகழப்படாமல் வாழ விரும்புபவன், எவ்வளவோ சிறியதாயினும் எந்தவொரு பொருளையும் திருட நினைக்காதவாறு தன் நெஞ்சைக் காக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet teaches that a respectable life requires strict inner discipline. The phrase 'எள்ளாமை வேண்டுவான்' describes someone who wishes to avoid being despised by society. To maintain this honor, he is instructed to guard his mind ('தன் நெஞ்சு காக்க') against the very thought of stealing ('கள்ளாமை'). The words 'எனைத்து ஒன்றும்' emphasize that this rule applies to absolutely anything, no matter how trivial, showing that true honesty is a state of mind before it is an action.

ai.literal: With the mind even thinking is evil indeed, another's property by deceit we will steal saying.
ai.translation: Even the mere thought of stealing another's property by deceit is an evil act.
ai.modern: மற்றொருவனுடைய பொருளை வஞ்சனையால் திருடுவோம் என்று மனத்தால் நினைப்பது கூடத் தீமையானதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes that the intention to commit a wrong is as bad as the act itself. The word 'உள்ளலும்' (even thinking) combined with 'உள்ளத்தால்' (with the mind) stresses that mental purity is essential. To say to oneself 'கள்வேம்' (we will steal) regarding another's property through deceit is declared to be 'தீதே' (evil indeed). Thus, true non-stealing begins in the mind, not just in physical actions.

ai.literal: Wealth accrued by theft, having exceeded the limit, will perish like it is growing.
ai.translation: Wealth accumulated through theft may seem to grow beyond all limits, but it will ultimately perish.
ai.modern: திருடுவதால் சேர்ந்த செல்வம், எல்லையைக் கடந்து பெருகுவது போலத் தோன்றினாலும், முடிவில் அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns about the deceptive nature of ill-gotten wealth. The word 'ஆக்கம்' generally means creation or increase, but here it specifically refers to wealth or prosperity. The phrase 'களவினால்' indicates that this wealth is acquired through stealing. Although such wealth might appear to grow boundlessly ('அளவு இறந்து ஆவது போல'), this growth is an illusion. The verse concludes with 'கெடும்', emphasizing that it will inevitably be destroyed.

ai.literal: Towards theft intense desire, in its result, unending sorrow will give.
ai.translation: An intense desire for theft will bring unending sorrow when it yields its results.
ai.modern: திருடுவதில் கொண்ட தீவிரமான ஆசை, அதன் முடிவில் அழியாத துன்பத்தைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the deep-seated urge to steal. The phrase 'களவின்கண் கன்றிய காதல்' describes a desire for theft that has grown intense and deeply rooted in a person's mind. While the act might seem appealing initially, 'விளைவின்கண்' points to the inevitable consequences that follow. The result is 'வீயா விழுமம்', which means a sorrow that never perishes or fades away. Thus, the desire to steal ultimately rewards the thief with endless suffering.

ai.literal: Compassion considering, love possessors becoming; wealth desiring, negligence watchers with, is not.
ai.translation: The state of being loving and valuing compassion is not found in those who covet wealth and watch for others' unguarded moments.
ai.modern: அருளை மதித்து அன்புடையவராக வாழும் தன்மை, பிறருடைய பொருளை விரும்பி அவர்கள் ஏமாந்திருக்கும் நேரத்தை எதிர்பார்த்து இருப்பவர்களிடம் இருக்காது.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the virtues of compassion and love with the predatory nature of a thief. The phrase 'அருள் கருதி அன்புடையர் ஆதல்' describes a life guided by empathy and affection for others. In contrast, 'பொருள் கருதிப் பொச்சாப்புப் பார்ப்பார்' refers to those who covet others' wealth and wait for a moment of negligence or vulnerability to steal it. The word 'இல்' firmly states that these two mindsets cannot coexist; a person scheming to exploit others' unguarded moments cannot possess genuine love or compassion.

ai.translation: Those who have an intense desire for theft cannot stand firm and conduct themselves within proper bounds.
ai.modern: திருடுவதில் மிகுந்த ஆசை கொண்டவர்கள், சரியான நெறிமுறையின் எல்லையில் நின்று வாழும் திறனற்றவர்கள் ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how the desire to steal corrupts a person's overall conduct. The word 'அளவு' refers to the proper limits or boundaries of righteous behavior. Those described as having an intense, deep-rooted craving for theft are consumed by this desire. Consequently, they lose the ability to stand firm and live within the bounds of a measured, ethical life.

ai.literal: Theft which is called dark-knowledge boldness, measure which is called power with those who practice is not.
ai.translation: The foolish boldness of dark ignorance known as theft is not found in those who practice the strong discipline of knowing their proper limits.
ai.modern: அளவு என்னும் வரம்பினை அறிந்து வாழும் ஆற்றல் உடையவர்களிடத்தில், களவு என்று சொல்லப்படும் மயங்கிய அறிவினால் வரும் துணிவு இருக்காது.
ai.explanation: The couplet contrasts two qualities: the disciplined strength of knowing one's proper limits ('measure') and the foolish boldness of stealing ('dark ignorance'). The word 'அளவு' (measure) refers to the boundary of what rightfully belongs to oneself, while 'காரறிவு' (dark knowledge) describes a mind clouded by greed. The author explains that those who possess the true power of self-restraint will never harbor the ignorant audacity to commit theft.

ai.translation: Just as virtue abides in the hearts of those who know their limits, deceit abides in the hearts of those who know theft.
ai.modern: தங்கள் அளவை அறிந்து வாழ்பவர்களின் நெஞ்சில் அறம் நிலைத்து நிற்பது போல, திருடுவதை அறிந்தவர்களின் நெஞ்சில் வஞ்சனை நிலைத்து நிற்கும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet contrasts two types of people and what resides in their hearts. For those who know their proper measure and limits, virtue stands firmly in their minds. In the same way, for those who are familiar with theft, deceit and concealment constantly occupy their thoughts. The word 'கரவு' means deceit or hiding, showing that a thief's mind is always troubled by the need to conceal their actions.

ai.literal: Measure not-things having done right-there they-will-perish, theft not other-things those-who-do-not-know.
ai.translation: Those who know no ways of life other than theft will commit boundless wrongs and perish right there.
ai.modern: களவைத் தவிர வேறு நல்ல வழிகளை அறியாதவர்கள், அளவுக்கு மீறிய தீய செயல்களைச் செய்து அப்போதே அழிந்து போவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the inevitable ruin that comes to those whose only skill is stealing. The phrase 'களவு அல்ல மற்றைய தேற்றாதவர்' refers to people who do not know any honest means of living, knowing nothing but theft. Because they lack moral boundaries, they commit 'அளவு அல்ல'—acts that go beyond all acceptable limits or measures. Consequently, 'ஆங்கே வீவர்' indicates they will perish immediately or right in the midst of their boundless transgressions.

ai.literal: To those who steal, the state of life will fail; to those who steal [error for: do not steal], the world of gods will not fail.
ai.translation: For those who steal, their very existence will fail them. But for those who do not steal, the celestial world of the gods will never fail.
ai.modern: பிறர் பொருளைத் திருடுபவர்களுக்கு அவர்களின் உயிரும் உடம்பும் நிலைக்காமல் அழிந்து போகும். திருடாதவர்களுக்குத் தேவர்களது உலகம் தவறாமல் கிடைக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the ultimate fates of thieves and honest people. Note that the provided text contains typographical errors: the second 'கள்வார்க்கு' (to those who steal) should be 'கள்ளார்க்கு' (to those who do not steal), and 'உளகு' should be 'உலகு' (world). The poet warns that for those who steal, even their 'உயிர்நிலை' (the state of life, or the body that holds life) will eventually fail and perish. In contrast, for those who maintain their integrity and do not steal, the heavenly world of the gods ('புத்தேள் உலகு') will never fail to welcome them.
